comparison: Both evaluate behavioral discrimination claims C11-C18. OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests and clear metrics. Peer reviewers find it UNCERTAIN, questioning the reaction time analysis methodology and requesting additional reporting of distributions, noting 'the use of discrimination time is uncommon in literature.'

Both evaluate correlation analysis claims C33-C35. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with good Boltzmann fits and statistical validation, noting the interpretation remains correlational. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, describing the data as 'nicely quantified' with 'very clear' maps and good signal-to-noise, with no concerns raised.

Both evaluate respiratory confound claims C60-C65. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting convergent evidence that breathing changes don't explain plasticity. Peer reviewers remain UNCERTAIN despite the data, stating 'no evidence shows sniffing affects signals, no evidence shows that it does not' and emphasizing this is 'the central conclusion' requiring more experimental evidence or balanced discussion.

Both evaluate distinction from developmental plasticity claims C38-C41. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting valid distinction between adult functional potentiation and developmental refinement. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging results are 'quite interesting since most work has focused on plasticity in central rather than peripheral processing.'

Both evaluate IOS signal source claims C49-C52. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate literature citations and acknowledgment of limitations. Peer reviewers find UNCERTAIN, explicitly challenging the interpretation: 'the signal source of ISI is ambiguous' and 'this issue is not completely resolved,' requesting more balanced discussion of signal sources.

Both evaluate speculative mechanism claims C53-C56. OpenEval finds UNCERTAIN, noting mechanisms are plausible but not directly tested. Peer reviewers find SUPPORTED but request 'more balanced' discussion given ambiguity about signal sources, suggesting mechanisms should be presented with appropriate caveats.

Both evaluate background/literature characterization claims C3-C10. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting accurate characterization of the field and knowledge gap. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, explicitly acknowledging that 'most work has focused on plasticity in central rather than peripheral processing,' supporting the authors' framing.

Both address IOS imaging claims, with OpenEval evaluating C19-C24 (trained vs naive vs exposed groups) and peer reviewers evaluating overlapping claims C20-C24 plus broader claims C1-C2, C26-C32. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong controls. Peer reviewers find UNCERTAIN, questioning whether potentiation reflects neural processing or sniffing behavior changes, and challenging the passive exposure control methodology.

OpenEval evaluates comprehensive IOS amplitude measurements C25-C32 as SUPPORTED with critical controls. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping claims C26-C32 (plus C1-C2, C20-C24) as UNCERTAIN, expressing major concerns about interpretation and whether changes reflect neural processing versus sensory sampling behavior.

Both address passive exposure controls. OpenEval evaluates C25-C32 as SUPPORTED, noting lack of difference between naive and exposed groups as critical control. Peer reviewers evaluate C25 and C43 as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether 'dilutions of odors reaching the nose in these two situations are equivalent' due to methodological differences in odor delivery.

Both address main conclusions. OpenEval evaluates C1, C2, C32 as SUPPORTED, noting convergent evidence for learning-specific long-lasting potentiation. Peer reviewers evaluate these claims (plus C20-C24, C26-C31) as UNCERTAIN, finding results 'very intriguing' but expressing major concerns about whether potentiation reflects neural changes or sniffing behavior.

Both address interpretive claims about behavioral implications. OpenEval evaluates C36-C37, C66-C67 as UNCERTAIN, noting improved detection is plausible but not directly tested. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping claims C36-C37, C66-C69 as SUPPORTED, not challenging these interpretations as speculative extensions of the findings.

Both address reinforcement-dependent plasticity claims C42, C46. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting appropriate acknowledgment of literature discrepancies and demonstrated generalization. Peer reviewers find UNCERTAIN, noting the finding is 'very intriguing' but questioning the passive exposure control methodology that underlies the reinforcement-dependence conclusion.

Both address passive exposure methodology. OpenEval evaluates C42-C46 as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate comparison of trained vs exposed groups. Peer reviewers evaluate C25, C43 as UNCERTAIN, raising substantial concerns about whether odor concentrations and sniffing behavior are equivalent between passive exposure and training conditions.

Both address cross-species implications. OpenEval evaluates C68-C69 as UNCERTAIN, noting human expertise claims are highly speculative despite appropriate citations. Peer reviewers evaluate C36-C37, C66-C69 as SUPPORTED, not challenging these as reasonable speculative extensions and implications of the findings.

OpenEval evaluates C47-C48 (contrasting findings with prior literature and speculation about inhibitory neurons) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations and identification of speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates C70-C71 (methodological details about animal age, sex, strain, purity) as SUPPORTED with adequate documentation for reproducibility. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details.

OpenEval evaluates C57-C59 (respiratory modulation confound from literature) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations establishing the potential confound. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims about respiratory effects.
